newsitem.title: USA: China's rating unaffected by Deng's death -Moody's.
newsitem.headline: China's rating unaffected by Deng's death -Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service on Wednesday said the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping should not affect the direction of China's economic policy and will have no impact on its A3 sovereign ceiling rating.
Moody's said it had already accounted for Deng's eventual demise in its assessment of China's credit.

"Deng has really not been in effective command of the country for a number of years now and the troika of leaders are pretty well entrenched at this point," said Hannan Salem, senior analyst with Moody's sovereign risk unit.
That transition also means the direction of China's economic policies should be unaffected, Salem said.
Tom Byrne, also a senior analyst with Moody's, said the "smooth" transition should manifest itself beyond the near term given the country's current positive economic trend.
"Things are going fairly well for the Chinese," Byrne said. "There are structural problems they have to deal with, but maybe now they'll start to deal with them with some uncertainty out of the way."
